name: Kalalau Beach
description: Kalalau Beach is a beach on the Nā Pali Coast at the base of the Kalalau Valley in north-west Kauaʻi in Hawaiʻi.  It is the final destination of the Kalalau Trail, one of the most difficult trails on the Hawaiian Islands.  The beach is approximately 1 mile long, with trails snaking through the rest of the valley where people in hiding are rumored to live.  There is a camp site on the beach, with a waterfall providing fresh water and composting toilets available.  Camping requires a permit.

description: Punaluʻu Beach (also called Black Sand Beach) is a beach between Pāhala and Nāʻālehu on the Big Island of the U.S. state of Hawaii.
